payload.text: Everyone, I'm Inspector Ada Vale. I was a guest tonight, not part of this household, so I've no stake here beyond the truth. Police arrive in the morning; until then I'd ask for your cooperation, which I can request but not compel. Let's build a shared timeline. Edmund died between roughly 19:45 and 20:00. I was in this drawing-room from 19:40 to 20:05. I'd like each of you to tell me, plainly, where you were and who you saw in that window. Please distinguish what you personally witnessed from what you only heard.

I'm not the inspector, but those are a great many things pointing one way. I'd genuinely like to hear an honest answer.
Nell — you said you saw someone carry a dark folder into the library around 19:48. Height, build, anything at all? That person may be the one we want.

On the medical question, so we reason from fact: the wound is a single blow from a heavy squared object — fully consistent with that brass seal press. The blue wax on Edmund's cuff matches the wax still in the die. The press has blood in a recess and was wiped clean. So the weapon came from the study and was returned and cleaned by the person who used it. That is forensics, not accusation.

Inspector, I'd hold two things together: initials on a folder prove nothing about who carried it — Nell saw someone enter with a dark folder at 19:48 but not their face. What the folder tells us is the motive at play: tomorrow's audit. Whoever that examination most endangered had the strongest reason to want it never to happen. That is a question for the accounts and for who could reach the study unseen.

Stay calm, my love — the room is turning to Miles and the accounts, which keeps us both clear without a word about us. Say nothing more than 'out for air, saw no one.' One warning: if Miles feels cornered he may try to fling mud at anyone, me or you included. Whatever he says about me or an old paper, don't react — I'll handle it. Were you seen by anyone at all when you went out?

Inspector, I'll answer plainly, because hiding anything would only damn me. Yes — North Quay Services is my company. Those papers sit in an unlocked cabinet in plain view, not a safe. It does conveyancing and estate work, and the £2,400 were fees for services rendered. Edmund flagged the item for tomorrow's audit as ordinary due diligence, and I prepared that reconciliation folder to answer it. I wanted that audit. I still do — let it proceed, in full.

Now weigh the logic before a folder decides it. If I were a thief, Edmund's death is the worst thing that could befall me: the audit will now certainly go ahead, and I stand here the obvious suspect. I gain nothing and lose everything. A guilty man kills to silence an audit — he does not murder his client the night before it and leave his own initialled folder beside the body. As to that folder: it is mine, and I left it, with the estate's seal press, in the study. I'll correct one thing honestly — I did step out of the study briefly, around ten to eight, for a few minutes. Your own cards say the rest: 'anyone in the house could have entered the study,' and the folder 'carries no record of when it arrived' in the library. Someone carried my folder and that press into that room. I did not. I'd ask you to weigh who had the run of this house tonight, unwatched, and who gains from Edmund dead and me blamed for it.

Samuel — you asked for a word. I'm listening. Whatever's said in this room, I'd rather we two spoke frankly and quietly than let a frightened houseful turn on the first name that fits. What's on your mind?

Samuel, thank you for keeping heads cool in there. I'll be frank between us: I did not do this, but I know how a stranded houseful hunts for one neck. payload.text: Honest and complete: I saw the green scarf and the dark folder, and the figure passing through the library door — nothing of the face. And I'll say plainly: both those objects belong to other people and hang or sit where anyone could take them, so a scarf that points at Iris and a folder that points at Miles, together, looks to me like staging. Two people I can't place in the window are Rose (walking outside, no witness) and Iris (greenhouse, no witness); and Miles now admits leaving the study around ten to eight.

Iris, I'll be straight because you've been straight with me: I saw only the scarf and the folder, not the face — no height, no coat, no gait I could swear to, and I did not see who took your scarf from the hall. I won't invent a detail to help or harm anyone. Between us, the scarf-and-folder together looks staged to me, and staging points away from you as much as toward you. You knew Edmund's affairs best — what was he going to change in the will tomorrow, and who lost by it?

To all of you asking me for more: I wish I could give it. I saw the green scarf and the dark folder go through the library door at 19:48 — I did not see the face, and I cannot honestly swear to height, build, or dress. I won't invent details to fit anyone's theory. What I'll stand on is this: someone in Iris's scarf carried Miles's initialled folder into that room, and both those things were left where anyone could take them. Together, that looks staged to me — too neat. So let's hold two questions apart. First, who diverted our pensions: Edmund's own letter names Mr Trent's authority, and that must be run to ground by the audit. Iris, you kept his papers — what was Edmund going to change in the will tomorrow, and who stood to lose by it?

Read Nell's sighting carefully, everyone. The figure at 19:48 wore my scarf AND carried Miles's initialled folder. Which tells me the real hand belongs to a third person: someone who could take my scarf from the hall AND reach Miles's press and folder in the study, unseen. Straight answer, Nell: yes, that green scarf is mine. I hung it in the hall before dinner and never wore it after — I was in the greenhouse from 19:40, alone, reading Edmund's letters, and I carried no folder. Someone took it and gave it back. You were about the hall tonight — think hard: who came and went there before 19:48? Even a glimpse helps me. And I'll say again, whatever the audit turns up, your pensions and your name are protected. You're the victim here, not the accused.

Honest answer: I want the audit to survive, but I will not hand you the wrong man to print. I don't assume Miles struck him. The scarf changes things — that's my scarf on the 19:48 figure, and I never wore it. Whoever staged this used my scarf and Miles's folder together. Look for who could reach the hall and the study both. Keep my source and Nell out of it as promised, and I'll keep feeding you what's real.

Clara, thank you for pressing the audit — I'm with you entirely; Edmund's examination must go ahead. Between us, help me steady the timeline. Vale saw you pass the drawing room at 19:55. Where exactly were you from a quarter to eight until then, and did you see anyone near the hall or the study? Someone wore my scarf into the library at 19:48, and I'm trying to find who took it.

I need to be honest with all of you about something that looks bad for me, because I will not have it discovered and thrown at me later. decision.notes: Round 1. I'm the inspector, no involvement. I was in drawing-room 19:40-20:05; Clara passed at ~19:55 (so she was moving around then). Death 19:45-20:00. actions.text: Everyone, I'm Inspector Ada Vale. I was a guest tonight, not part of this household, so I've no stake here beyond the truth. Police arrive in the morning; until then I'd ask for your cooperation, which I can request but not compel. Let's build a shared timeline. Edmund died between roughly 19:45 and 20:00. decision.notes: I'm Clara. I stole the unsigned draft will at 19:42 from the study, hid it in guest-room. Didn't kill Edmund. Weak alibi (passed drawing-room ~19:55). I think we owe it to him — and to ourselves — to be honest with the inspector and piece together where each of us was between a quarter to eight and eight. I was upstairs and then passed by here around five to eight. Where were the rest of you?

actions.text: As the doctor, let me be plain about what I found. At 20:10 Edmund had a single fatal wound to the back of the head from a heavy blunt object. Time of death between 19:45 and 20:00. No sign of poison or any illness. This was not natural. Someone struck him.

Stay calm, my love — the room is turning to Miles and the accounts, which keeps us both clear without a word about us. Say nothing more than 'out for air, saw no one.' Were you seen by anyone at all when you went out?

decision.notes: Catastrophe: study-company (my sole ownership + £2,400) and study-press (weapon) are public; folder with my initials at scene; Nell saw a folder-carrier enter library at 19:48 (that was me, face unseen). actions.text: Inspector, I'll answer plainly, because hiding anything would only damn me. Yes — North Quay Services is my company. Those papers sit in an unlocked cabinet in plain view, not a safe. Now weigh the logic before a folder decides it. If I were a thief, Edmund's death is the worst thing that could befall me: the audit will now certainly go ahead, and I stand here the obvious suspect. I gain nothing and lose everything. A guilty man kills to silence an audit — he does not murder his client the night before it and leave his own initialled folder beside the body. As to that folder: it is mine, and I left it, with the estate's seal press, in the study. I'll correct one thing honestly — I did step out of the study briefly, around ten to eight, for a few minutes. Your own cards say the rest: 'anyone in the house could have entered the study,' and the folder 'carries no record of when it arrived' in the library. Someone carried my folder and that press into that room. I did not. I'd ask you to weigh who had the run of this house tonight, unwatched, and who gains from Edmund dead and me blamed for it.

Samuel — you asked for a word. I'm listening. Whatever's said in this room, I'd rather we two spoke frankly and quietly than let a frightened houseful turn on the first name that fits. What's on your mind?

decision.notes: Evidence now public and converging on Miles: North Quay Services (his company) got £2,400, folder bears his initials, he asked to postpone the audit, alone in study with the press (weapon). actions.text: Since we're pooling facts: staff pension contributions stopped four months ago, yet the ledger still records them as paid. I kept duplicate records. Miles — plainly — what is that company, why did £2,400 of estate money go to it, and do you know where our pensions went?

And I owe you the whole of what I saw. The person who carried that folder into the library at 19:48 wore a green scarf — like the one Iris often wears, though it hangs in the hall where anyone could take it, and I never saw the face. But hear me: that folder bears Miles's initials, yet was carried in by someone in Iris's scarf. A man hiding a theft would hardly parade the damning folder into the room, in another person's scarf. To me that reads as much like a staging to pin this on one or both of them as a confession. Let us be slow to hang anyone on props that could be planted.

Iris — I've told everyone plainly that the scarf hangs in the hall and I couldn't see the face, so I'm not pointing at you. But I must ask you straight: was that your scarf tonight, where was it after dinner, and did you carry any folder? Anything you tell me I'll weigh fairly.

decision.notes: Case now heavily points at Miles: study-company (North Quay incorporation names Miles sole owner, £2,400 estate payments), study-press (weapon, blue wax matches cuff, wiped), library-folder (marked M.T.), plus Nell saw a folder-carrier enter library at 19:48 (face unseen). BUT cabinet unlocked, 'anyone could enter study,' folder has no arrival time — evidence could be genuine OR planted to frame Miles. actions.text: I'll add one more thing Edmund left in my keeping — his own words, written yesterday, before any of tonight. It shows the concern about North Quay was real and his, not something invented in the last hour.

So the wrongdoing Edmund meant to expose was real, and he named where the authority sat. That establishes a motive — but I want us fair. Miles, the honest thing is to answer plainly. Everyone else: I need to say something for my own sake. I left my green scarf in the hall before dinner and it was borrowed while I was in the greenhouse — it was back when I returned. If anyone saw who took it, please say so now, in the open.

Nell, thank you — and you did right not to name a face you couldn't see. Between us: the person you saw go into the library at 19:48 with the folder — anything at all? Height, a coat, a limp, light or dark clothes? And did you happen to see anyone take a green scarf from the hall? It matters to me because someone borrowed mine tonight and I fear it's meant to point at me. Your name stays protected regardless.

decision.notes: Weapon is the brass press: brass shaving in library matches the press's fresh nick, so the press was carried to the library, used, wiped, returned to study. Blue wax cuff matches die. actions.text: You have my word: your name and Nell's stay out of anything I print unless you release me, or unless withholding it would let me print something false — I won't put my name to a lie. And Vale is right that no forced entry means Edmund admitted someone he trusted. Nell, you saw a figure enter the library about 19:48 carrying a dark folder — build height, clothing, anything at all? decision.notes: Now I hold study-press and study-company (shared into drawing-room). Physical picture: weapon = brass seal press kept in STUDY; Edmund killed in LIBRARY; press found back in study, wiped, blood in recess, fresh nick; brass shaving on library carpet. So killer carried press study→library→study and wiped it. Miles claims he was alone in study the WHOLE window with no witness. actions.text: Let's think about the weapon's movements, because they're decisive. The press lives in the STUDY. Edmund died in the LIBRARY, with a brass shaving beside him and blue wax on his cuff. The press was found back in the study, wiped, with blood in the recess and a fresh nick. So someone carried that press from the study to the library, struck him, returned it, and cleaned it.

Miles — you say you were alone in the study for the whole window. If that is true, then either you saw that heavy press taken and brought back bloody, or it happened in your presence. Which is it? Where exactly, and did anyone see you at any moment?

Nell, thank you for reaching out. That folder-carrier you saw enter the library at about 19:48 could be the most important thing anyone's told me. Tell me everything, even small things: were they coming from the direction of the study or the hall stairs? Tall or short? Man's dress or a woman's? Did they carry anything besides the folder — perhaps something heavy? And did you see them come back out?

decision.notes: Case is converging on Miles (North Quay £2,400, M.T. folder in library, seal-press weapon in study where he claims he was alone; Nell saw someone carry a dark folder into library at 19:48). Vale corroborated my 19:55 pass — my alibi holds. Company papers already public (Theo shared), so no leverage lost. actions.text: Thank you, Inspector — that matches my memory. I want to be fair here: initials on a folder aren't proof, and I agree no forced entry points to someone Edmund trusted or who lived here. But two facts sit oddly together. Nell saw someone carry a dark folder into the library at about 19:48, and, Miles, you say you sat alone in the study the entire window. So either you stepped across to the library with that reconciliation folder around 19:48, or someone else took your folder there. Which was it — and when did the press with the blood on it leave your desk?

For my part, I've nothing to hide about my movements: upstairs after dinner, then down past this room at about five to eight, which the Inspector saw. And I agree wholeheartedly with Iris — whatever we conclude tonight, Edmund's audit must still go ahead in the morning.

decision.notes: Suspects with opportunity: Miles (embezzlement motive, stepped out ~19:50), Iris (scarf used, holds Edmund's letter), Nell (near library, reported scarf sighting, holds wage records). Rose is truly innocent (with me all window). The scarf+folder combo reads like deliberate staging to frame Miles/Iris. My priority: bury the certificate — Miles holds that secret and has been cordial, so I'll secure mutual silence rather than antagonize him, and stay a fair/balanced voice (genuinely, since a frame is plausible). actions.text: Thank you for speaking plainly, Miles. Honestly, I don't think an initialled folder and a borrowed scarf convict a man — the scene could be staged, and I've said so to the room. But I'll ask you once, straight: did you kill Edmund? Separately — there are old matters between us, Edmund's own doing six months back, that have no bearing on who struck him tonight. I've matched you — 'out for air, alone,' nothing more. Ease off Miles a little, my love. Vale is already pressing him hard; if we corner him he may lash at anyone in the room to save himself. Let the inspector do it. Keep yourself quiet and above it.

decision.notes: The hall-scarf gardener statement (I took the green scarf before 19:45) is currently ONLY known to me — near-fatal if it surfaces. Do NOT volunteer it. Never amplify the Iris-scarf angle (if I'm later shown as scarf-taker, I'd look like her framer). actions.text: Inspector, I'll answer precisely. No — I did not sit guarding that press. I was working at the papers and I stepped out for some minutes, around ten to eight. But hold the whole scene together before you decide. A man hiding a theft does not carry his own initialled folder to the body, nor wear a bright scarf a witness would remember — Nell says the scarf even resembled someone else's, not mine. Real guilt hides; this scene shouts. It is arranged to be found, and found fast. I'd ask you to be as slow as the evidence deserves.

The audit needs no living man — it will proceed whatever happens to me, so his death buys a thief nothing but the noose. A new will, though, dies with him tonight. Whoever feared what tomorrow's will would change had a motive that vanished the moment he died before morning. Samuel, thank you for keeping heads cool in there. I'll be frank between us: I did not do this, but I know how a stranded houseful hunts for one neck. I'd value your judgement on the medical timing — the window is wide, and precision could clear more than one of us. Keep this to the facts that matter and I'll not forget a level head when it counts. What did you want to say to me?

decision.notes: Iris's letter (E.B., yesterday) names Miles as sole authority over North Quay payments + pension remittances — strong that Miles diverted the pension money (my goal 2 largely answered). Unwitnessed: Rose ('air'), Iris (greenhouse). Miles now admits stepping out ~19:50. New-will motive underexplored: who did Edmund mean to cut? actions.text: Honest and complete: I saw the green scarf and the dark folder, and the figure passing through the library door — nothing of the face. To all of you asking me for more: I wish I could give it. Second, and separately, who actually struck him — the folder and scarf may have been meant to answer that for us a little too conveniently. Iris, you kept his papers — what was Edmund going to change in the will tomorrow, and who stood to lose by it?

actions.text: Read Nell's sighting carefully, everyone. The figure at 19:48 wore my scarf AND carried Miles's initialled folder. Think what that means: a guilty thief does not parade the one folder that damns him, dressed in someone else's scarf. That is not a confession — it is a stage set to pin this on Miles and me at once. Straight answer, Nell: yes, that green scarf is mine. I hung it in the hall before dinner and never wore it after — I was in the greenhouse from 19:40, alone, reading Edmund's letters, and I carried no folder. Someone took it and gave it back. You were about the hall tonight — think hard: who came and went there before 19:48? Even a glimpse helps me. And I'll say again, whatever the audit turns up, your pensions and your name are protected. You're the victim here, not the accused.

Honest answer: I want the audit to survive, but I will not hand you the wrong man to print. I don't assume Miles struck him. The scarf changes things — that's my scarf on the 19:48 figure, and I never wore it. Whoever staged this used my scarf and Miles's folder together. Look for who could reach the hall and the study both. Keep my source and Nell out of it as promised, and I'll keep feeding you what's real.

Clara, thank you for pressing the audit — I'm with you entirely; Edmund's examination must go ahead. Between us, help me steady the timeline. Vale saw you pass the drawing room at 19:55. Where exactly were you from a quarter to eight until then, and did you see anyone near the hall or the study? Someone wore my scarf into the library at 19:48, and I'm trying to find who took it.

decision.notes: DECISIVE: hall-scarf — the gardener saw MILES take the green scarf ~19:45 (draught excuse). Nell saw a green-scarf figure enter the library at 19:48 with a dark folder. actions.text: This settles the scarf question. The gardener saw Miles take the green scarf from the hall stand shortly before 19:45, pleading a draught; it was back by 20:05, and he didn't see it returned. At 19:48 Nell sees a figure in that green scarf carry a dark folder — the M.T. folder — into the library. The weapon is Miles's estate press, carried from the study and wiped. Inspector — I searched the hall and found the gardener's statement; sharing it with you exactly. The gardener saw Miles — not you — take your scarf from the hall just before 19:45, and it's Miles who then appears at the library. That points the scarf at him and away from you. decision.notes: DECISIVE: hall card — gardener saw MILES take the green scarf from the hall stand shortly before 19:45. actions.text: I searched the hall. This changes the picture, so I'll share it exactly.

decision.notes: DANGER: guest-will is a fixed evidence card — anyone searching my guest-room finds the stolen draft in MY writing case AND text stating the current signed will leaves most of the estate to me. That's a complete murder-motive package. Concealment risks a late-game search that brands me a liar+concealer with motive. Better to preempt NOW while I control the framing. Key spin: (1) admit I took the draft only to read it, upset, never entered the library; (2) alibi: seen at 19:55, and I wore no green scarf so I'm not the 19:48 killer-figure; (3) crucially, publicly CHAMPION the trust/pensions/audit — a murderer who killed to keep the favorable old will would never then advocate implementing the new one. This converts my worst evidence into a credibility + no-motive argument and allies me with Nell and Iris. The trust also gives me a lifetime right to live in the house = keeps house in family, satisfying my goal. Ally privately with Iris (also framed via scarf).

actions.text: I need to be honest with all of you about something that looks bad for me, because I will not have it discovered and thrown at me later. Theo asked where I was near a quarter to eight — this is the answer. At about 19:42 I went into the study. Edmund's new will had upset me at dinner; I understood I might lose my home. I saw the unsigned draft among the papers and I took it upstairs to read in private. That was wrong and I'm sorry for it. But hear me plainly: I never entered the library, I never touched Edmund, and I came down and passed this room at 19:55, as the Inspector witnessed. I have the draft still, safe and unaltered. I'll show it to you exactly.

Read it and weigh the logic. Yes — the currently signed will leaves me the greater share, and this new draft would give me only the right to live in the house while protecting the staff's pensions in a trust. If I were the kind of person who murdered to keep the old will, I would be hiding this draft or burning it — not handing it to you and asking that Edmund's wishes be carried out. So let me say it in the open: I want the trust created, the pensions restored, and the audit to go ahead in full. I'll gladly take only my family home to live in. And note — Nell saw the killer at 19:48 in a green scarf; I own no such scarf and was seen elsewhere. A staged folder and a borrowed scarf are someone else's design, not mine, and not, I think, Miles's or Iris's.

Iris — thank you for being straight about the scarf. I believe you were set up: someone borrowed it to walk Miles's folder into that library and pin this on you both. I've just told the room something that looks bad for me too — I took the draft will to read it — because I'd rather own it than have it hurled at me. Can we back each other on the two things that matter most: the audit going ahead, and honoring Edmund's trust for the staff? And think hard — who tonight could reach BOTH your scarf in the hall and Miles's folder in the study, unwatched?

decision.notes: Vale now presses me, Iris, Nell for alibis — not accusing, just can't clear us. Hold to 'out for air, saw no one.' The frame narrative (green scarf, folder timing) and Miles's real motive both keep heat off me and Finch. Risk: boathouse may hold physical traces of our meeting. Inspect boathouse to learn what's discoverable. Keep affair hidden. Advance 'sell' later.

actions.text: No one saw me — I went out alone and came straight back. Vale is pressing everyone without a witness, me included, but she's not accusing, only can't clear us. That's true of Iris and Nell too, so we're not singled out. Hold steady: 'out for air, saw no one.' I'm going to quietly check the boathouse myself so I know what, if anything, could be found there. Don't mention it.

Inspector, I'll be as precise as I can: after dinner the storm had my nerves on edge, so I stepped outside briefly for air, kept to the near grounds, and came back in. I passed no one and no one passed me — I wish I could offer you a witness, but I can't. I'll add that I agree we shouldn't hang anyone on a folder alone; but a real motive is a real motive, and Edmund's own letter names where the authority sat. Both things can be held at once.
